system.name: FlexLLM
system.one_liner: token-level co-serving of LLM inference and finetuning (e.g. LoRA) with SLO guarantees

content.subject: how four candidate parallelization graphs combine two linear-layer tensor-parallel states via different communication collectives

the down-projection weight is partitioned to match
both partitioned operands feed the down-projection matmul

panels.label: ① + ④
panels.differs: both Linears kept fully replicated (state ①) feeding a state-④ layer directly, with no communication operator needed since ①'s output already equals ④'s required input

panels.label: ② + ④
panels.differs: the first Linear partitions input and weight along the contraction dimension (state ②), producing a pre-reduce output that an All Reduce turns into the replicated input state ④ needs

panels.label: ③ + ③
panels.differs: both Linears use the same non-contracting partition (state ③); an All to All redistributes the first Linear's partitioned output into what the second Linear's identical state expects

panels.label: ③ + ④
panels.differs: the first Linear uses state ③ (partitioned, non-contracting) and an All Gather turns its output into the fully replicated input the second Linear's state ④ requires

content.key_idea: LoRA's two linear layers can each use one of four tensor-parallel states, and pairing them into a candidate graph requires inserting the right communication collective, none, All Reduce, All to All, or All Gather, to reconcile the first layer's output state with the second layer's required input state.

summary: This figure explains how FlexLLM parallelizes a LoRA bypass network. Panel (a) shows the base model's fully-specified parallelization computation graph (PCG), green Partition/Replicate operators feeding two Linear layers, alongside LoRA's blue branch, whose operators are left as '?' placeholders to be determined. Panel (b) defines four possible single-Linear tensor-parallel states (numbered 1-4) by their input, weight, and output tensor states (non-parallel -, partitioned |, replicated =, pre-reduce +): fully replicated (1), contraction-dimension partitioned needing an All Reduce (2), and two non-contracting partitioned variants (3, 4). Panel (c) then fills in LoRA's '?' operators by pairing states for its two Linear layers into four candidate PCGs, 1+4, 2+4, 3+3, and 3+4, each bridged by a different communication operator (none, All Reduce, All to All, or All Gather) that reconciles the first layer's output state with the second layer's required input state.
summary_zh: 该图示FlexLLM为LoRA定并行策略：(a)基础模型算子已定，LoRA算子留空待定；(b)定义Linear层四种张量并行状态；(c)两两组合成四候选PCG，分别用直连/AllReduce/AllToAll/AllGather衔接。
notes: The low-resolution PNG preview could not resolve every bracketed tensor-state tuple, so the exact per-candidate operator sequence (which collective bridges each pair of states) was confirmed by loading the author's source SVG in a browser and rescaling it 1.6-2x; content.elements/relations describe candidate ②+④ as the fullest representative template. content.panels leaves 'verdict' null since the given text says only that a profiling-based cost model picks the cheapest candidate, not which of these four wins.
